title: The five non-negotiable skills for AI architects
oneliner: Know your cloud's AI services, know the LLMs you will actually use, know containers - the non-negotiable base for AI architects in 2026.
says: His non-negotiables: know the AI services of your cloud of choice (watsonx on IBM Cloud; SageMaker and Bedrock on AWS); know the LLMs your project uses or plans to use (IBM's Granite, AWS's models, or open-source models on Hugging Face); and know containerization, because that is how these workloads actually run.
explained: The pattern in the list is 'your stack, concretely.' Not AI services in general - the ones on the cloud your employer runs. Not LLMs in the abstract - the specific models your projects will call, with their limits and costs. This is what separates an architect from an enthusiast: decisions are made against a real stack with real constraints.

Containerization makes the list because AI workloads ship like everything else: packaged, orchestrated, and scaled as containers. An AI architect who cannot reason about how the model server is deployed, scaled, and isolated is designing in the air. The open-source-model point matters too - knowing what Hugging Face offers keeps you from defaulting to the most expensive hosted option for every problem.
takeaway: Audit yourself against the stack you actually work on: its AI services, its models, its container platform. Generic AI knowledge is not the job.
